sections.title: Martech Market Overview
sections.body: The marketing technology market reached $48.2 billion in 2026 and is compounding at 14.3% annually, on track for $78 billion by 2031, driven by AI-powered tools, customer data platforms, and the continued expansion of content marketing operations. The average marketing team runs 11.8 distinct SaaS tools, with larger organizations exceeding 20, and marketing's share of total software budget has held near 26% — high and stable relative to other departments. The structural shift is compositional rather than total: budgets are moving from broad suites toward specialized best-of-breed tools, particularly in analytics, personalization, and AI content. For buyers that reallocate rather than add, the stable budget share means consolidation savings can fund the AI stack — a point CFOs respond to much better than incremental tool-by-tool approvals.

sections.title: AI Adoption in Marketing

stats.label: Marketing Budget Spent on AI Tools
Marketers Reporting AI Improves Output Quality
Time Saved on Content Creation with AI

sections.body: Marketing is the front line of AI adoption: 52% of teams now use AI-powered content creation tools, and marketing departments lead all functions in AI spend at 28% of their budget. The results justify the allocation in the way buyers care about: 73% of marketers report that AI improves output quality, 44% report time savings on content creation, and 38% of enterprise marketing content is now AI-generated. The most common use cases are content generation, campaign personalization, predictive analytics, and audience segmentation — the same categories that dominate vendor roadmaps in 2026. The caveat in the data is the quality claim's dependency: the 73% quality-improvement figure is reported overwhelmingly by teams that combine AI drafting with human review, and the gap between AI-assisted and AI-replaced workflows is where the quality and brand-safety differences actually show up.

Average Cost per Click (Google Ads, All Industries)

sections.body: Channel benchmarks in 2026 confirm where the economic center of gravity sits: email delivers a 6.4x average ROI — the strongest of any paid or owned channel — on a 3.2% average conversion rate, while search ads convert at 5.7% on premium pricing of $5.78 average cost per click, and social advertising trails at 1.9% click-through. Those three numbers frame the media plan trade-offs every CMO faces: email is the compounding asset that rewards list quality and segmentation work, search is the highest-intent but most bid-up exposure, and social CTRs have declined as platform algorithms weight user-generated content and organic engagement. For teams benchmarking their own performance, industry-level averages like these are a sanity check, not a target — list quality alone moves email conversion by multiples, so the correct comparison is against your segment's own baseline, not all industries combined.

sections.title: Marketing Stack Complexity

stats.label: Leaders Citing Data Integration as Top Challenge
Reduction in Tool Count After Stack Consolidation

sections.body: The enterprise martech stack has become a small software estate: the average enterprise counts 1,632 components once plugins, integrations, and point solutions are catalogued, at an average annual spend of $1.2 million. Utilization is the industry's persistent problem — only 41% of martech capabilities are actively used — and 74% of marketing leaders name data integration across the stack as their top operational challenge. The corrective is measurable: organizations that run stack audits and rationalize tooling reduce their counts by an average of 23% while maintaining or improving performance, largely by killing redundant point tools and routing data through one integration layer. Buyers should treat the 41% utilization figure as a procurement checklist item — a new tool should demonstrably replace or retire an existing component, not add to the 59% of shelfware that drags down integration velocity and per-tool ROI.
